Must possess valid California Driver's License to drive a County or University vehicle. Ability and means to travel on a flexible schedule as needed, proof of liability damage insurance on vehicle used is required. Reimbursement of job-related travel will be reimbursed according to University policies.
High school diploma or equivalent experience.
Administration and Support:

Provide support for program activities by using computer to assist with workload of advisors and/or program staff; provide overall program support using copier for program materials, correspondence via email and telephone calls.

Arranges meetings with internal staff and external groups. Performs meeting arrangements including facilities, audio/visual equipment services and catering services. Compiles appropriate records, e.g. receipts, contracts, set-up and process online credit card registrations, statements for payment, and reimbursement. Assists in processing professional continuing education units and educational materials, printed materials, research papers and agendas.
Establish in-house procedures and guidelines.
Assist in the preparation of materials for trainings, workshops, and events.

Prepare travel, purchase orders, check requests, deposits, donations, correspondence, newsletters, forms, reports, tables, and other documents using word processing, spreadsheet, and graphics software from draft through final versions. Review and edit documents for grammar, punctuation and spelling, enhance and maintain web pages, determine and ensure documents are in appropriate format in accordance with department style manual.
Provide general program support to staff.
Develop and maintain website for the Capitol Corridor Multi-County Partnership and programs. Working with staff, develop and disseminate press releases to support program outreach and delivery.
Provide General Administrative Duties:
Answer general phone lines, route callers to appropriate parties, provide general program and procedural information. Problem-solve clientele issues before forwarding to program staff.
Assist with personnel activities including preparation of related correspondence and forms as needed.
Maintain a variety of databases.

Thorough knowledge of Microsoft Office, knowledge of modern office equipment (phone systems, laptops, sound equipment, etc.), modern office practices and procedures. Knowledge of style/format of business correspondence, punctuation, and general English usage. Compose correspondence independently.

Ability to organize work effectively to meet critical administrative deadlines and determine office priorities. Manage routine projects without constant supervision. Ability to work cooperatively with co-workers and community partners; reliable, efficient and honest.

Work in a regular office environment. Have word processing skills; database skills, ability to maintain database; and general office experience. Competency and practical experience in basic computer issues and desktop publishing.

Skills to organize work effectively, to achieve timely progress on multiple simultaneous projects, distribute effort appropriately among the projects, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of productivity.
Writing, editing and proofreading skills to prepare a variety of correspondence, reports and written procedures.
Experience developing and maintaining websites.
Special Conditions of Employment:
Overtime and occasional weekend work as needed, usually on short notice to meet operational needs may be requested.

As of January 1, 2014, ANR is a smoke- and tobacco-free environment in which smoking, the use of smokeless tobacco products, and the use of unregulated nicotine products (e-cigarettes), is strictly prohibited.
